in_text_mentions: A previously healthy, immunocompetent four-year-old girl presented to the emergency department with fever, malaise and several blistering lesions that appeared after two days of pain and erythema in the neck and extremities. The lesions started as flaccid bullae that desquamated and afterwards crusted. They were localized in the neck, extremities and perioral and periorbital areas, with copious purulent secretions around the nares and eyes. All the lesions were painful and desquamated when pressure was applied (positive Nikolsky sign) (Figure 1).

plate_findings.evidence: superficial epidermal desquamation along the eyebrow region
Perioral skin involvement with erythematous patches and superficial erosions extending to the vermilion border

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real clinical photograph of a human patient's periocular region showing bilateral eyelid edema, erythema and superficial epidermal desquamation of the eyebrows, captioned as ocular manifestations at presentation in a case report of staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome; the periorificial onset pattern is a recognized less-common (variant) presentation. B: Real clinical photograph of a human patient's perioral region showing erythematous patches, superficial erosions and desquamation extending to the vermilion border with buccal mucosal erosions, captioned as perioral involvement at presentation in staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome; periorificial disease is a recognized less-common (variant) pattern.
panels.attribution_text: Troisi et al. Case report: Eyelid symptoms as an early harbinger of staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome: a novel pattern of disease onset.. Frontiers in ophthalmology 2025. doi:10.3389/fopht.2025.1689008. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Ocular and perioral manifestations at presentation. (A) Bilateral eyelid edema and erythema with superficial epidermal desquamation along the eyebrow region, associated with patient discomfort and difficulty keeping the eyes open. (B) Perioral skin involvement with erythematous patches and superficial erosions extending to the vermilion border, accompanied by erosive lesions of the buccal mucosa.
in_text_mentions: open, and evident desquamation of the skin near the eyebrows in both eyes. A corneal fluorescein staining test (fluotest) was performed at the bedside using a binocular ophthalmoscope with a cobalt blue filter after gentle manual eyelid retraction. The result was negative in both eyes, ruling out epithelial corneal defects at presentation. On inspection of the face, erythematous-desquamative lesions similar to those in the periocular region were also noted in the perioral skin, with extension to the buccal mucosa (Figure 3). Posterior segment evaluation was entirely unremarkable in both eyes.
